title: Climate and market shocks drive productive diversification and income resilience in Chilean small-scale fisheries
content:
Abstract
This study analyses how climate and market shocks drive diversification strategies in Chilean small-scale fisheries (SSF) and their effects on household income. Using panel data (1998–2022) from CASEN surveys, fisheries landings, and environmental indices, we estimate instrumental variable models within a sustainable livelihoods and site assessment framework. The analysis operates at two complementary levels: a commune-year panel model, which captures how local fishing portfolio diversification responds to environmental variability (ENOS), declining resource abundance (CPUE), and first-sale prices; and a household-level cross-sectional model, which examines how diversification strategies are associated with income across heterogeneous fishing households. Results from the commune-level model show that fisheries diversification responds significantly to environmental variability (ENOS), declining resource abundance (CPUE), and market price signals, with notable regional variation—the central macrozone exhibits particularly strong climate-driven diversification responses. At the household level, diversification is positively associated with income, yet its effectiveness varies systematically across household types. Fishing-dependent households benefit more from income diversification beyond fisheries, while households with broader livelihood portfolios gain more from within-fisheries diversification. Regional heterogeneity is pronounced: central macrozones show lower incomes and greater climate-driven diversification, whereas northern regions exhibit mixed responses. Community-level economic diversification reduces diversification in fisheries, suggesting substitution effects. These findings highlight that diversification is an adaptive response to exogenous shocks, but its outcomes depend on household capabilities, spatial context, and local opportunity structures. Understanding these dynamics is essential for designing effective policies that enhance resilience and reduce vulnerability in SSFs facing growing environmental and economic pressures.
